eismeer-hagenbeck.title: Arctic Ocean
text: With a footprint of around 7,700 m² and a volume of approximately 27,700 m³, the facility recreates the polar coastal regions of the Antarctic, the Arctic and Patagonia through massive, artificially modelled rocks and bays. It is home to polar bears (Ursus maritimus), walruses (Odobenus rosmarus), various seal species, subtropical and Antarctic penguins, and Arctic seabirds.

Tradition and innovation form the cornerstones of the concept for the reconstruction of this historic facility. The listed, dilapidated structure was replaced by a new construction that takes its cue from the original appearance. Alongside exceeding the strict EU requirements and best-practice standards for animal husbandry, the central aim was to give visitors a deeper understanding of the fascination of the animals and their habitats.

The visitor route leads through the different habitats of the Arctic, the Antarctic and Patagonia. Generous panoramic windows open up striking views into the underwater worlds, while barrier-free visitor areas and an innovative educational concept provide additional information on ecological, biological and global interrelationships.

A particular highlight is the Antarctic penguin enclosure within the “Ice Chamber”, where authentic rock structures and permanently low temperatures of below 7 °C create a natural habitat. It is home to a colony of king penguins (Aptenodytes patagonicus) and gentoo penguins (Pygoscelis papua), which the innovative design of the enclosure encourages to engage in a wide range of activity such as walking, climbing, swimming and sliding.
A sustainable water and energy concept ensures that 5.5 million litres of water are cooled to a constant maximum of 15 °C and enables almost carbon-neutral operation of the entire facility.

tropen-aquarium-hagenbeck.title: Tropical Aquarium
facts: 1,700 m³ deep-sea tank, panoramic window 15 × 7.5 m
text: The Tropical Aquarium is one of the outstanding projects of modern zoo architecture. Covering an area of around 7,800 m², the building extends over several levels and offers a unique visitor experience – on foot, directly beneath free-flying birds and bats, and in the midst of tropical animal worlds.

The central challenge was to develop exhibition concepts for reptiles, amphibians and small mammals that, in line with the vision of Carl Hagenbeck, the inventor of the moated enclosure, allow a seemingly barrier-free presentation. The upper levels, with their dense tropical vegetation, show a wide variety of tropical and subtropical habitats. They house an African safari lodge, a tropical village, one of the largest indoor crocodile lakes in the world, a mangrove swamp and numerous smaller habitats for small mammals, reptiles, insects and arachnids.

From the upper areas of the tropical forest, the visitor route leads through a bat cave and a venomous snake village down into the subterranean part of the building – the aquarium. Here visitors encounter impressive marine and freshwater worlds with living corals, anemone cylinders, lionfish, moray eels, an Amazon tank and jellyfish kreisels. The centrepiece is the 1,700 m³ deep-sea tank with sharks and rays, which can be viewed from the auditorium through a panoramic window 15 metres wide and 7.5 metres high.
The building incorporates numerous innovative solutions for optimising water and energy use. For its unique sustainability concept, the Tropical Aquarium received an environmental award in 2009.

orang-utan-dome-hagenbeck.title: Orang-Utan-Dome
facts: Three quarters of the dome opens in 7 minutes
ETFE membrane on a rotating tubular steel structure
text: The concept of the building is based on the idea of a weather-protected outdoor exhibit. The orangutan rainforest house at Tierpark Hagenbeck, measuring around 1,000 m², allows three quarters of the roof dome to be opened within just seven minutes. This enables both the animals and the visitors to experience the natural outdoor climate. The ETFE membrane is mounted on a rotating tubular steel structure, allowing the roof to be opened and closed flexibly. When closed, temperature and humidity are precisely regulated to create optimal conditions for animals and plants.

A water moat serves as a natural barrier between animals and visitors while allowing unobstructed sightlines. Individually developed, flexible climbing elements offer the Sumatran orangutans (Pongo abelii) a wide range of opportunities for movement. The facility is complemented by innovative enrichment devices and by mixed-species housing with Asian small-clawed otters (Aonyx cinerea), which provide additional variety and occupation.
The modern, functional architecture promotes the animals’ well-being and creates a visitor experience that is as fascinating as it is close to nature.

polarium-rostock.title: Polarium
text: Opened in 1969, the polar bear enclosure at Rostock Zoo was considered one of the most modern of its kind at the time and led to numerous breeding successes. This successful tradition is also the origin of the zoo’s choice of the polar bear as its logo, as well as its long-standing management of the International Studbook. After more than five decades, however, the enclosure no longer met today’s requirements for animal husbandry and visitor experience.

In order to create a forward-looking polar bear breeding facility appropriate to the species, a Europe-wide competition was launched in 2016, which also included the redesign of the adjacent Humboldt penguin enclosure.

The resulting concept combines the latest findings in breeding and husbandry practice with a sensitive integration into the urban surroundings. Differently designed habitats offer the animals a great deal of variety and freedom of movement, while visitors enjoy an intense animal experience through naturalistic design and a wide range of views. The “Polarium” visitor centre complements the facility with interactive and educational exhibitions, underwater views and aquariums that vividly convey life at the poles.
The project was successfully opened in 2018, in time for Rostock’s 800th anniversary.

artenschutz-aquarium-schoenbrunn.title: Species Conservation Aquarium
text: Together with Wehdorn Architekten – as joint-venture partner for site supervision – the Europe-wide competition was won. The new building is to blend sensitively into the historic ensemble of the Tiergarten and present the underwater world in all its uniqueness. A meandering visitor route around 400 metres long, weather-independent and barrier-free, leads through the newly created underwater world.

The central attractions are large-scale tanks for the Amazon, corals and sharks, as well as jellyfish kreisels and a tunnel tank. Breathtaking freshwater and deep-sea experiences are staged and presented in a unique way.
A new central square and Tiergarten shop closely link the aquarium with the overall visit to the Tiergarten, so that it remains an integral part of the experience.
artenschutz-aquarium-schoenbrunn.scope: Overall project management, HOAI work stages 1–9, general planning, HOAI work stages 1–7, joint-venture partner Wehdorn Architekten, work stages 8–9 & construction health and safety coordination (BauKG)
artenschutz-aquarium-schoenbrunn.alt: Species Conservation Aquarium, Tiergarten Schönbrunn, Vienna

haus-der-giganten-verona.title: House of Giants
text: The ageing tropical house at the heart of the privately run Parco Natura Viva in Italy lies in the middle of a protected landscape area and on the border between two municipalities. On the basis of grandfathering rights and an initial conceptual approach, the construction of a new hall was approved. This was followed by the planning and design of the entire facility – from the selection of animals and enclosure design, through water and building services, to visitor circulation and the management areas behind the scenes.

In close collaboration with the client and the local planning and zoological team, the new “House of Giants” attraction was created. The visitor route leads through different habitats of the largest representatives of the world of birds, reptiles, amphibians, fish and insects – including the giant otter, native to the Amazon.

The naturalistic design of the habitats and the route along boardwalks and through themed huts create an impressive visitor experience in which the boundaries between people and animals visually blur and the fascination of tropical biodiversity becomes tangible.
haus-der-giganten-verona.alt: House of Giants, Parco Natura Viva, Verona

elefantenfreilaufhalle-hagenbeck.title: Elephant Free-Roaming Hall
text: The design of modern elephant facilities follows the highest standards and combines visitor appeal with optimal conditions for the husbandry, breeding and well-being of this highly social species. The naturalistic habitat offers the animals everything they need for a healthy, active life and for successful reproduction and rearing, while at the same time giving visitors an impressive and authentic experience.

The planning and construction of such facilities require specialist knowledge of elephant management and a deep understanding of the biology of these animals. Tierpark Hagenbeck was the first zoological institution to successfully enable an elephant birth within the herd in human care. The Elephant Free-Roaming Hall designed for this purpose was tailored specifically to it and opened in 2006. Covering an area of around 1,000 m², it provides generous areas for movement and variable functional zones that allow natural social behaviour.
Several calves have already been born in this facility within the stable herd structure and raised naturally by their mothers and relatives.
elefantenfreilaufhalle-hagenbeck.alt: Elephant Free-Roaming Hall, Tierpark Hagenbeck, Hamburg

masterplan-2030-koeln.title: Masterplan 2030
text: As part of Masterplan 2030, Cologne Zoo is undergoing comprehensive development in technical, operational and architectural terms. The aim is to promote animal welfare and the animal experience through generous, authentically designed communal enclosures in which different species are kept together in a true-to-nature way. The result is an incomparable and contemporary zoo experience.

New sightlines and perspectives open up through low-lying, panoramic enclosure structures that accompany the visitor route in a special way. Generous walk-through free-flight aviaries allow direct immersion in the habitat and let visitors become part of the shared living space.
The phased implementation of the individual projects ensures continuous visitor operation and a smooth visitor route throughout the entire development process.

kaenguruhaus-hagenbeck.title: Kangaroo House and Outdoor Enclosure
text: The aim of the project was to redesign the existing outdoor enclosure for Australian mammals and birds in accordance with the historic “Hagenbeck standard” of open moated enclosures. Covering an area of around 750 m², a modern facility was created that combines tradition with contemporary animal husbandry. In addition, a new heated house was built, offering both animals and visitors a sheltered and appealing place to spend time on rainy days.

The outdoor enclosure is divided into two separable areas with open moats, allowing flexible husbandry and varied management of different species. The new house is accessible to visitors and is inhabited by free-flying birds and roaming wallabies (Macropus rufogriseus). Through an open viewing window, the imposing red kangaroos (Macropus rufus) can be observed seemingly without barriers.
The facility opened in 2011 and has since offered a naturalistic and lively experience of Australian wildlife.
kaenguruhaus-hagenbeck.alt: Kangaroo House and Outdoor Enclosure, Tierpark Hagenbeck, Hamburg

dickhaeuterhaus-tierpark-berlin.title: Pachyderm House
facts: Free-roaming hall with ETFE foil cushion roof
text: With its imposing size and a footprint of around 7,000 square metres, the “Pachyderm House” at Tierpark Berlin, opened in 1989, is one of the significant buildings of its time. Alongside African and Asian elephants, it has so far also housed Indian rhinoceroses and manatees, presented in a classic linear stable structure.

A comprehensive modernisation and redesign of the house is now planned, turning it into a contemporary and sustainable overall facility dedicated primarily to keeping African elephants. The existing building will be embedded in a naturalistic and authentically designed African experience area. A reorganisation of the interior will significantly improve husbandry conditions and create more space for movement and enrichment. The light-filled free-roaming hall with ETFE foil cushion roof, natural sand floor, bathing pool and a wide range of enrichment options enables a varied presentation appropriate to the species.
Quote from Dr Knieriem, Director of Tierpark Berlin: “The new elephant house will be an important milestone not only for Tierpark Berlin, but for elephant husbandry throughout Europe.”

The visitor area will also be developed into an experience space in its own right. Barrier-free habitats for small mammals, reptiles and birds along the route enrich the visit and make it attractive even when the elephants are not on view.

inselzoo-altenburg.title: Inselzoo Masterplan
text: A holistic concept was drawn up for the further development of the Inselzoo as a public institution. In collaboration with Pluswerte, analyses, surveys of the existing site and visitor surveys were carried out, which formed the basis of the masterplan. The findings gave rise to key thematic focal points: a waterfowl aviary with an integrated lighthouse, a Madagascar lemur island, an adventure playground and covered seating areas overlooking the attractions, designed as places to discover, experience and linger.

giraffenanlage-koeln.title: Giraffe Enclosure
text: On the basis of Masterplan 2030, developed together with Cologne Zoo, the existing giraffe enclosure is being comprehensively modernised in order to meet the revised husbandry guidelines and enable sustainable, future-oriented animal husbandry. The mixed-species housing with gazelles and antelopes will be retained as it is today.

A generous free-roaming hall with natural flooring is planned, offering a wide range of husbandry and movement options. As an innovative solution, almost the entire building façade can be opened to the outdoor enclosure via sectional doors, creating a fluid, barrier-free transition between inside and outside.
The outdoor enclosure will be enlarged by relocating the barrier-free visitor path and, in its final state, will cover an area of around 2,300 m².

nashorngehege-koeln.title: Rhino Enclosure
text: On the basis of the revised husbandry guidelines for rhinoceroses, the existing bison and musk ox enclosure at Cologne Zoo is being converted, sustainably and with a view to the future, for keeping rhinoceroses.

As part of the project, enlarged visitor and enclosure areas are being created. Existing timber log cabins are being converted and upgraded into weatherproof stables with due regard to heritage conservation. In addition to the visitor path, three generous, barrier-free visitor terraces for lingering and observing are being created – one of them fully roofed.

robbenanlage-rostock.title: Seal Enclosure
text: As the ageing seal enclosure had structural, functional and, above all, energy-related deficiencies, the existing facility was replaced by a modern and sustainable new one.
A modern habitat appropriate to the species, which at the same time offers visitors a special experience, was planned.

direktorenvilla-koeln.title: Director’s Villa
text: Together with the South America House and the Antelope House, the Director’s Villa is one of the oldest buildings from the zoo’s founding period and remains a defining part of the historic ensemble.

The historic building was carefully refurbished and opened to the public. Today it houses, among other things, catering facilities and combines historic charm with new functionality, not least through its distinctive interior design.
direktorenvilla-koeln.scope: Architecture & landscape, HOAI work stages 5–7, interior design, HOAI work stages 1–7

stadion-meeressaeuger-asien.title: Marine Mammal Stadium
text: A design was developed for a novel presentation and husbandry facility for marine mammals. The concept defines an entirely new form of animal husbandry that permanently allows the animals a species-appropriate “migration” through a generous infinity pool. Complementary research and education facilities, above and below water, complete the holistic concept and combine scientific insight with a sustainable experience space.

elefantenwelt-wilhelma.title: Elephant World
text: A competition was launched for the new “Elephant World” at the Wilhelma in Stuttgart. The aim was to design an additional entrance, a new restaurant and an elephant facility unique of its kind within the historic park with its characteristic paths and sightlines.

The design produced an innovative concept for keeping a “multi-generation” elephant herd that surpasses existing best-practice approaches while being sustainable and economically viable to operate. In urban design terms, the facility was sensitively embedded in the park and complemented by clear, understated architecture whose construction makes it as functional as it is atmospheric and suited to the animals.
The result is a forward-looking concept that is convincing in terms of zoological husbandry as well as economy, functionality and design quality.

asien-anlage-opel-zoo.title: Asia Exhibit
text: The Opel-Zoo is planning to convert the existing giraffe enclosure and the enclosures for elands, Prince Alfred’s deer and blackbucks into a modern and future-oriented Asia exhibit. Plans include a walk-through heated house for Indian rhinoceroses and Malayan tapirs, as well as a viewing stable for siamangs. A new kiosk with a viewing terrace overlooking the rhino house completes the concept.

As part of the restricted competition, a design was developed that responds to the extremely steep slope and integrates the heated house with different access levels. The building was given a functional and understated design and geared towards sustainable operation. In addition, varied and naturalistic outdoor enclosures were conceived. The visitor paths lead through the facility on different levels, creating an authentic and intense experience of nature.
asien-anlage-opel-zoo.alt: Asia Exhibit, Opel-Zoo, Kronberg im Taunus

eisbaerenanlage-wuppertal.title: Polar Bear Enclosure Redesign
text: In 1911, the “Nordlandpanorama” (Northern Panorama) was presented to the public at today’s Wuppertal Zoo, then the Elberfeld Zoo. Impressive artificial rock landscapes and a unique panorama allowed visitors to observe polar bears, sea lions and mountain goats at the same time. The founder of the Hamburg Tierpark, Carl Hagenbeck (1844–1913), advised the zoo at the time on the construction of this impressive facility.

Today there are plans to fundamentally redesign the existing polar bear enclosure and the seal enclosure in front of it, or to give them a new use. The aim is to develop an innovative concept based on modern “best practice” animal husbandry, possibly with an adapted animal collection. The new facility is to blend harmoniously into its surroundings and offer visitors an attractive, educational and future-oriented experience.
eisbaerenanlage-wuppertal.alt: Polar Bear Enclosure Redesign, Zoo Wuppertal, Wuppertal

artenschutz-uwec-uganda.title: Nature and Species Conservation Project
text: As an ongoing commitment, the Uganda Wildlife and Education Centre (UWEC) in Entebbe, Uganda, has been supported financially.

Uganda – the “Pearl of Africa” – is one of the continent’s biodiversity hotspots and is home to some of the rarest animal species in the world. Alongside the critically endangered mountain gorilla, the endangered shoebill also lives in the country’s extensive wetlands.

Through its extensive environmental education and teaching programmes, UWEC makes an important contribution to raising the younger generation’s awareness of the protection of wildlife and its habitats. The institution is also involved in active species conservation: in its integrated animal clinic, injured native animals receive veterinary care and are subsequently released back into the wild.
The financial support has made possible numerous smaller projects, repairs and construction works that secure the continued existence and further development of the institution.
artenschutz-uwec-uganda.alt: Nature and Species Conservation Project, Uganda Wildlife Education Centre (UWEC), Entebbe

aqua-park-vae.title: Aqua Park Masterplan
text: For a client from the United Arab Emirates, a concept for a “Swimming Zoo” with an affiliated nature conservation centre – the first of its kind worldwide – was developed. In addition to high leisure and recreational value thanks to its attractive overall design, the concept is distinguished by a hitherto unique form of animal presentation in which the boundaries of the enclosures visually disappear under water.

The particular climatic and cultural conditions of the site were taken into account in the selection of animals and the design of the enclosures. The aim was to create an innovative concept that goes beyond existing European and American standards in zoo animal husbandry and enables participation in international conservation breeding programmes.
The seemingly direct contact between people and animals makes the “Swimming Zoo” a unique experience space and an outstanding unique selling point for the future operator.

suedamerikahaus-koeln.title: South America House
text: Together with the Antelope House and the Director’s Villa, the South America House is one of the oldest buildings from the zoo’s founding period and remains a defining part of the historic ensemble. Framed by trees, the building’s formal language is modelled on a Russian Orthodox church.

As part of a comprehensive core refurbishment of the listed building, the detailed design, the tendering and award of construction works and the interior design were carried out. The building, formerly used as a bird house, has been brought back to life and is now home to various South American species. At its centre, a planted free-flight and walk-through area was created, extending from the basement floor up to the translucent ETFE foil roof and creating a natural, open spatial atmosphere.
suedamerikahaus-koeln.scope: Architecture & landscape, HOAI work stage 5 (partial revision & interior design) & work stages 6–8
suedamerikahaus-koeln.alt: South America House, Cologne Zoo, Cologne

biodome-budapest.title: Biodome
text: In Budapest, a unique project is taking shape with the so-called “Biodome”: a covered zoo being developed together with the local general planning team Mertek. The aim is to present native and historical biodiversity in a weather-independent environment. The spectacular building envelope, a self-supporting transparent structure, sets new standards for European zoo architecture.

In the course of the design planning, the planning and operational requirements for animal husbandry, operation and construction were defined in close coordination with the architects and engineers. The result is a concept that unites functional, technical and zoological aspects in a holistic, forward-looking approach.

onagergehege-hagenbeck.title: Onager Enclosure
text: One of the first enclosures on the route through Tierpark Hagenbeck is the onager enclosure, which presents this rare and highly endangered species of wild ass all year round.

Through a targeted reshaping of the terrain, the outdoor enclosure was modelled so that the animals can be experienced on different levels and from different perspectives. This spatial layering gives visitors the impression that the onagers and the camels kept behind them share a common habitat, even though the two species are separated by invisible moats.

Beneath authentic-looking rock formations lie feeding zones and shady retreats, while open areas and several circular routes provide ample space for movement and withdrawal. The result is a naturalistic and varied habitat that promotes both the well-being of the animals and the visitor experience.

baerengehege-hagenbeck.title: Bear Enclosure Extension
text: The aim of the project was to modernise the historic bear enclosure located directly at the old Art Nouveau entrance. The challenge lay in developing a modern, functional breeding facility for large bears on the site of a listed facility.

In addition to the renewal of the indoor areas – including backstage areas, dens and breeding dens – an additional enclosure was created in front of the historic one. A wide water moat gives visitors unobstructed views into the naturalistic landscape and its imposing inhabitants. Two separate outdoor enclosures, which can be connected via a swing bridge invisible to visitors, allow the keepers to separate animals when necessary, while visitors are given the impression of a single continuous area.
Kamchatka brown bears (Ursus arctos piscator) are successfully bred and raised naturally in the facility.
baerengehege-hagenbeck.alt: Bear Enclosure Extension, Tierpark Hagenbeck, Hamburg

elefantenbullenkraal-hagenbeck.title: Elephant Bull Kraal with PC Wall
text: In accordance with EAZA and AZA guidelines, elephant bulls are kept under so-called “Protected Contact” (PC). Against this background, the elephant bull facility at Tierpark Hagenbeck was modernised to ensure safe, weather-independent care that is at the same time suited to the animal.

In close collaboration with the internationally recognised elephant expert Alan Roocroft, an innovative “PC wall” was created that gives the bull sufficient space to cooperate while providing the keepers with a protected working area. This system allows all necessary care and health procedures to be carried out safely while giving the animal full attention and individual care.
elefantenbullenkraal-hagenbeck.alt: Elephant Bull Kraal with PC Wall, Tierpark Hagenbeck, Hamburg

elefantenpark-zuerich.title: Elephant House and Enclosure
text: The competition was subject to a fixed budget and left no room for elaborate architecture. On an area of around 11,000 m², the focus was therefore on developing a functional concept that enables future-oriented husbandry and efficient management of this valuable species.

The innovative and pioneering result was developed in close collaboration with international specialists, whose expertise contributed decisively to the development of a sustainable and practice-oriented overall concept.
elefantenpark-zuerich.alt: Elephant House and Enclosure, Zurich Zoo, Zurich

elefanten-badeteich-hagenbeck.title: Elephant Bathing Pool
facts: Refurbishment of the historic elephant enclosure from 1923
text: As part of the refurbishment of the historic elephant enclosure, built in 1923, a newly designed elephant bathing pool was created at Tierpark Hagenbeck. The result is a naturalistically modelled pool for Asian elephants that encourages the animals not only to bathe but also to dive.

Gently sloping banks allow safe entry and exit, especially for elephant calves. The landscaped surroundings, planted on the visitor side, offer spectacular views of the animals’ bathing behaviour. Without visible barriers, visitors experience these impressive scenes at close range – an authentic and fascinating example of modern animal enclosure design.
elefanten-badeteich-hagenbeck.alt: Elephant Bathing Pool, Tierpark Hagenbeck, Hamburg

onager-zuchtzentren-iran.title: Ex-situ Onager Breeding Centres
text: The onager is one of the critically endangered animal species and today occurs only in a few regions of the arid semi-deserts of the Islamic Republic of Iran. To secure the population in the long term, the Iranian Department of Environment initiated the establishment of an ex-situ breeding group of this rare species of wild ass.

As part of this important species conservation project, experience from ex-situ management in the husbandry and breeding of these equids is being contributed. On this basis, a detailed concept for the establishment and design of the new breeding stations is being developed, contributing to the conservation and stabilisation of the species in human care.

gondwana-tropenhalle-leipzig.title: Gondwana Tropical Hall
text: As part of its masterplan, Zoo Leipzig launched a competition for the design and concept of the world’s largest tropical hall. A generous restaurant and events area was to be integrated as part of this unique zoological facility.

Within the interdisciplinary competition team, an innovative and coherent overall concept was developed that unites architectural quality, functional planning and economic efficiency and remains entirely within the specified budget.
gondwana-tropenhalle-leipzig.alt: Gondwana Tropical Hall, Zoo Leipzig, Leipzig

karawanserei-al-wabra.title: Al Wabra Caravanserai
text: A new concept for an education and research centre was developed for a private breeding facility with an exceptional collection of rare species. The design drew on the regional culture and led to the idea of a modern caravanserai – a place of encounter and exchange.
The result is a platform unique in the world that unites knowledge, research and education in a hospitable, inspiring and architecturally sophisticated setting.
karawanserei-al-wabra.alt: Al Wabra Caravanserai, Al Wabra Wildlife Preservation

pavilion-arctic-moskau.title: Pavilion Arctic
text: As part of the gradual modernisation of the historic Moscow Zoo, a new enclosure concept was developed for its flagship species, the polar bear. Taking into account the zoo’s long tradition and its central location in the middle of the city, two alternative concepts with different budgets were produced.

The planning is based on the latest findings in the husbandry and breeding of polar bears and provides for differently designed habitats that offer the animals varied enrichment and a naturalistic environment. For visitors, themed design and a wide range of views from different perspectives create an impressive and educational animal experience.
In addition, particular importance was attached to an integrated educational concept and to additional uses in the form of function and event spaces.

eisbaergehege-schoenbrunn.title: Polar Bear Enclosure
text: The polar bear enclosure at the heart of Tiergarten Schönbrunn, the oldest zoo in the world, was in need of refurbishment and was to be replaced by a modern, attractive and future-oriented breeding facility. On an area of around 3,400 m², a concept was developed that significantly improves the animals’ living conditions while creating an impressive visitor experience.

The competition entry was developed in close collaboration with habitat designers, taking into account all biological, zoological and technical requirements. The result is a concept that is both functional and sophisticated in design, and that remains precisely within the specified budget.
eisbaergehege-schoenbrunn.alt: Polar Bear Enclosure, Tiergarten Schönbrunn, Vienna

zoo-kaliningrad.title: Kaliningrad Zoo Redevelopment
text: In the course of its intended membership of EAZA (European Association of Zoos and Aquaria), the historic Kaliningrad Zoo, formerly the Königsberg Zoo, is to be comprehensively reorganised, modernised and redesigned. A local architecture practice was commissioned to draw up and implement a new masterplan. The planning team was additionally strengthened by specialist support and experience in the field of modern zoo architecture.

A particular challenge was the newly built but not yet opened primate facility, which had been realised with an investment of around 12 million euros. After completion, however, considerable functional and safety-related deficiencies became apparent that ruled out its use for the planned animal husbandry. A concept was therefore developed that allows an economically and technically sensible adaptation of the building, so that the facility can be used properly for the intended primate species.
zoo-kaliningrad.alt: Kaliningrad Zoo Redevelopment, Kaliningrad Zoo, Kaliningrad

nebeneingang-koeln.title: Side Entrance with Zoo Shop
text: As part of the implementation of Cologne Zoo’s Masterplan 2020, the side entrance on Riehler Gürtel was redesigned. In close collaboration with the zoo and under the project management of Dipl.-Ing. Sezai I. Candan, a new, functional concept was developed that modernised the existing entrance and enhanced its design.

On an area of around 250 m², the existing shop building was relocated, converted and transformed into an attractive side entrance with an integrated zoo shop. At the same time, the adjacent toilet facilities were renovated and redesigned in line with the zoo’s corporate identity. The project was completed and opened on schedule and within budget in summer 2014.
nebeneingang-koeln.alt: Side Entrance with Zoo Shop, Cologne Zoo, Cologne

doha-zoo-masterplan.title: Doha Zoo Masterplan
facts: Scenarios at 100, 250 and 500 million US dollars
text: On behalf of the Qatari Public Works Authority (ASHGHAL), a feasibility and masterplan study was prepared for the comprehensive refurbishment and redesign of Doha Zoo in Qatar. The concept for the site of around seventy hectares integrates elements of the existing zoo worth preserving and combines them with modern, sustainable planning approaches.

The study developed various future scenarios, including a safari landscape, a children’s farm, an indoor playground and a themed hotel. Animal husbandry adapted to the country’s extreme climatic conditions, a holistic educational concept and economically viable uses are central components of the masterplan.

Several implementation options with investment volumes of 100, 250 and 500 million US dollars were examined. A modular approach was recommended, starting with a smaller budget and allowing later expansion.
A key aspect of the planning was the development of a zoo concept usable all year round, as well as the spatial and functional integration of the new zoo into the adjacent sports park.
doha-zoo-masterplan.alt: Doha Zoo Masterplan, Doha Zoo, Doha

vielfrass-anlage-moskau.title: Wolverine Enclosure
text: A new concept was developed to optimise both visitor appeal and the daily workflows of animal care. Building on the existing structure, a solution was devised that can be implemented with manageable effort while enabling a significant functional improvement.

The result is a modern and appealing facility with optimised management areas for the native species, the wolverine. It combines efficiency in animal care with an attractive and naturalistic visitor experience.

clemenshof-koeln.title: Clemenshof Farm
text: Under the motto “Kölner Zoo 2020 – Begeistert für Tiere” (Cologne Zoo 2020 – Passionate about Animals), the new “Clemenshof” farm with an integrated zoo school, petting zoo and zoo shop was created as part of the masterplan.
The zoo shop and an exclusive events area were designed jointly and opened on schedule.

The Clemenshof is home to rare and native livestock breeds, kept in an authentically designed historic farmstead and its surroundings. The integrated zoo school gives pupils the opportunity to get to know animals and agriculture through direct experience.
clemenshof-koeln.scope: Architecture & landscape, interior design, HOAI work stages 5–8

zoologische-beratung-doha.title: Zoological Consulting
text: As part of the masterplan development for the new Doha Zoo, a detailed animal collection plan was drawn up, compiling all relevant information on the zoo’s future species. The species were selected on the basis of key criteria such as adaptability to extreme climatic conditions, educational value and importance for species conservation.
This comprehensive document serves as a guideline for future planners and contractors, establishing a clear framework at an early stage and avoiding errors in the subsequent detailed design.

As the implementation of the masterplan progressed, the Public Works Authority (ASHGHAL) commissioned specialist support for the zoological and veterinary assessment of the existing zoo. This involved both analysing the current animal collection and developing strategies to ensure the husbandry and care of the animals during the construction phase of the new zoo.

masterplan-erweiterung-sued-schoenbrunn.title: Masterplan Southern Extension
text: Under the direction of its Director, Dr Stephan Hering-Hagenbeck, Tiergarten Schönbrunn is planning its “Masterplan 2035”. ZQD GmbH had the privilege of providing planning support on various projects, including the concept for the “Southern Extension Area” (Phase 1). Being able to provide specialist support in developing the masterplan for the oldest zoological garden in the world was a unique opportunity, a special experience and a particular honour for us.
